note: The archive's other half. Ivan Defranceski of Crikvenica married Hedviga Blažević of Senj, and everything on this page stands behind her — a line of Senj carriers, tobacco-factory workers and Karlobag seafaring families that is, in the end, better documented and older than the Defranceschi spine itself.
lead: This archive was built around one surname and kept finding that the surname was the shallower half. Hedviga Blažević, who married Ivan Defranceski and died at Johannesburg in 2001, came from a Senj family whose registers run back without a break to the middle of the eighteenth century, and whose Karlobag branch reaches people born around 1690. Six photographs of register pages, taken at Senj in 2014 by a researcher the family engaged, and a MyHeritage ancestor chart for one woman, are all it took. Nobody had read them.

spine.who: Ivan Papić and Matija, born Pilipić
spine.what: Named as the parents in their son's baptism of 1857 and again in his marriage of 1885. Matija — Matia Papić as she became — was born at Karlobag on 18 September 1838 and died at Senj on 9 February 1886, four months before her granddaughter Milka was born. Her own ancestry is the deepest thing in this archive and is set out below.

Baptised at Senj on 1 November 1857 by Joannes Pisić, cooperator of the place — «Josephum filium legitimum Romano-Catholicum Joannis Papić et ejus uxoris Mathia Pilipić». Godparents Michael Slipomišić and Catharina Pasquan. He was a trhonoša, one of the Senj carriers, when he married and when his daughter was born; by 1907 the register calls him gostioničar, an innkeeper. He died on 19 November 1939, aged eighty-two.
Born at Krivi Put house 136 on 12 May 1859 and baptised there on the 15th, «Antonia Prpić, legitima», daughter of Ivan Prpić. She came down off the Velebit road into the town. Died 2 February 1935.

Born at Senj on 9 October 1886 and baptised on the 17th — entry 96, «Milka Lucia, zakonita», daughter of Josip Papić trhonoša and Tonka née Prpić. Both her godfather Josip Glavičić and her father are entered as trhonoše: two of the three men named in her baptism carried loads for a living. Eighty-five years later somebody came back to this page and wrote her death across the remarks column — 7 September 1971, from the Sveti Križ death register, entered by the registrar on the 30th.

Born at Senj on 8 March 1926, the daughter of Milka's second marriage. She married Ivan Defranceski of Crikvenica and died at Johannesburg on 30 October 2001 — six years to the day after he died at Senj.

milka.heading: Milka married twice, and the tobacco factory is in both entries

rows.w: Entry 30 of the Senj marriages. He is twenty-four, born 13 January 1883, «činovnik u tvornici duhana» — a clerk in the tobacco factory. She is twenty-one, «radnica u tvornici duhana» — a worker in the same factory. Her father is entered as gostioničar. They married by dispensation, the licence dated 3 November 1907.

rows.t: Milka marries Ljubomir Blažević, as a widow
rows.w: Entry 41. She is thirty-four and entered «udova». He is twenty-eight, born at Rijeka on 1 March 1892, living at Senj, unmarried; his parents Šime Blažević and Terezija née Zdunić are both recorded as dead. Her parents are given as Josip Papić and Antonija née Prpić. Witnesses: Franjo Đorić, tailor, and Mirko Trifun, innkeeper and tobacco-factory man. Married by Ivan Škrivanić, archpriest and registrar, under dispensation no. 3371.

rows.t: What is not in the file
rows.w: How and when Zvonimir Vukelić died. Between November 1907 and December 1920 fall the whole of the First World War and the influenza of 1918–19, and Senj lost heavily to both. The Senj death register for those years would answer it in an afternoon and nobody has looked.

trade.heading: Trhonoša
trade.text: The word is entered three times across these pages and it is not a general term for a labourer. The trhonoše of Senj were the carriers — the men who took goods up the Vratnik pass on packhorses, from the harbour into the Lika and the interior, and brought grain and timber down. Senj lived on that traffic for centuries; the town's whole reason for existing was that it was where the sea met the road over the Velebit. Josip Papić was one of them in 1885 and still one of them in 1886, and by 1907 he kept an inn — which, on that road, is the same business by other means.
trade.then: And his daughter went into the tobacco factory. The Senj tobacco works was the town's industrial employer, and both Milka and the man she married at twenty-one were in it. One generation from packhorse to production line.

karlobag.heading: Behind Matija: the Karlobag ancestry
karlobag.lead: A MyHeritage ancestor chart in the family's files, «Preci od Matia Papic», carries her line back five further generations, all at Karlobag on the Velebit channel. These are the oldest people the archive can name, and they are on the mother's side.

rows.who: Maria Pilipić, born Smojver, called Oliva
Catherina Pillipić, born Luckinić, called Catta
Oliva Smojver Vukić, born Bacchi, called Andreana
Lucia Gerkacs, born Tomljanović, called Maja
Vicentius Luckinić, called Vicko, and Maria Luckinić

karlobag.read: Nicolaus Gerkacs was born in 1717 and Josiph Smojver Vukić in 1731; the parents standing above them were born in the last years of the seventeenth century. Nothing on the Defranceschi side of this archive goes nearly so far — the documented spine there begins with a baptism of 1787. The names are the names of the Podgorje: Pilipić, Uroda, Gerkacs, Smojver Vukić, Luckinić, Tomljanović, Pekas — with one Italian among them, Caetano Bacchi, in a town that had been an Austrian free port since 1776. Two of them are placed not at Karlobag but at Montani Stanište up on the mountain, and one couple at Smiljan inland.
karlobag.caveat: This chart is a MyHeritage product and carries no citations on its face. Its dates are precise to the day and its month names are the Croatian ones, which points at somebody reading the Karlobag registers directly — and the family holds scans of Karlobag births 1691–1770 and 1804–1861 and the Karlobag Stanje duša. Treated here as good but unverified: the register images to check it against are already in the house.

correction.heading: A correction to the family's tree
correction.text: The MyHeritage GEDCOM gives Josip Papić's father as «Georgius Juraj (Joannis) Antić», born at Selce in 1838, with Matia Pilipić as his mother. He cannot be. The baptism of 1 November 1857 names the father as Joannes Papić and the child takes Papić; the marriage of 3 May 1885 names him again the same way. And an Antić born in 1838 would have been nineteen when the child was baptised — possible, but the register does not say it, and the register is the record. Josip Papić's father was Ivan Papić. The parenthesis «(Joannis)» sitting inside that Antić's name in the file looks like the seam where two men were merged.
correction.note: This is the second such splice found in the same file. See the Imotski page for the first, and for why they happen.
